newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court overrules B Band disqualification.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court overrules B Band disqualification.

text.p: A Brazilian high court judge Monday allowed a telecommunications group to continue bidding for B Band cellular telephone concessions, overruling a Communications Ministry decision to disqualify the group.
Judge Americo Luz of the Superior Justice Tribunal ruled the ministry had been "too excessive in its formalities" when it disqualified the Tess consortium from the B Band bidding procedure in June.
In a written statement, the judge said the group had been punished for using a translator who was not officially registered with the government and for other bureaucratic slips.

Citing the importance of attracting as many bidders as possible to the B Band program, Luz awarded Tess an injunction allowing it to continue in the bidding pending judgment of the merit of the group's appeal.
Tess comprises Swedish telecom group Telia along with construction group AR Almeida and Airline Cellular, both of Brazil.
It was one of five groups disqualified by the ministry for failing to meet technical criteria of the B Band bids. Minister Sergio Motta upheld the disqualifications Friday.
At least one other group banned from the bidding process has appealed with the Superior Justice Tribunal and others were reported to be preparing their appeals.

The moves come ahead of Wednesday's scheduled opening of price bids from groups seeking to win a 20-year concession to operate B Band cellular services in the Sao Paulo metropolitanm area, the most lucrative of 10 regional concessions on offer.
Bids for another concessions covering the states of Bahia and Sergipe were also due to be opened Wednesday.
The B Band program is the first phase of the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications program and is expected to net about $6.0 billion in license fees.
